title: Prompt Cost Forensics Panel & Pricing Slab Composer
creator: Emma Chen
description: Design prototype and interaction spec for a Prompt Cost Forensics Panel in Redwood Console. Purpose: give engineers and finance owners a fast, queryable view that traces token-level cost from API request -> model tokens -> pricing slab -> final invoice line. Includes an interactive waterfall that decomposes cost by token role (prompt/context/assistant), operation type (generation, embedding, rerank), route, and pricing slab (hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved vs private flat). Also includes a Pricing Slab Composer UI for mapping product SKUs and reserved commitments to per-token effective rates and exporting cost attribution as CSV/Parquet for downstream BI. This ticket covers the high-fidelity Figma prototype, UX flows for common tasks, acceptance criteria, and handoff artifacts for engineering and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive waterfall visualization that breaks a single API request into: input tokens, model generation tokens, system messages, and embeddings with per-token counts and micro-costs
Pricing Slab Composer that allows PMs and finance to define slabs (on-demand, reserved tiers, discounts) and preview effective per-token price across historical usage windows
Attribution export supports CSV and Parquet formats with schema: request_id, timestamp, route, user_id, model, role, token_count, token_type, unit_price, line_item, total_cost
UI performs queries against aggregated cost store within < 2s for 30-day window and provides a sampled mode for large ranges
Rollout integration: panel honors rollout pinned model versions and displays fallback events when model substitution occurred
Design tokens, spacing, colors, and components follow the Console design system; Figma and component spec attached for dev handoff
decisions: Use waterfall as primary visualization for single-request forensics and a stacked area for aggregate timelines
Expose 'role' (system, user, assistant, embedding) as first-class filter to match engineering mental model
Export formats chosen: CSV for quick analysis, Parquet for large-scale ingest by finance/BI teams
Pricing slabs modeled as ordered tiers with a fallback default rate; Composer will accept overrides for customer-reserved rates
Avoid exposing raw token content in UI for privacy; only token counts and pseudo-metrics are shown
open_questions: Should the Pricing Slab Composer support time-based rate changes (effective date ranges) or just static tiers?
What authorization boundary is needed for customers to edit slabs for Dedicated vs Hosted? (RBAC scope)
How to represent mixed-model requests where generation uses one model and embeddings use another in the waterfall?
Exact API contract for export: will the backend provide pre-aggregated rows per request or should the UI assemble rows from multiple endpoints?
